checklists.title: Gateway 1 readiness
checklists.intro: The five areas regulation 21(2) says the self-assessment summary must cover, with the progress MHCLG recommends in each before you start the 30 months. Tick what is true today; the count tells you how ready you are.

guidance.label: Getting ready: recommended progress by Gateway 1

items.text: The first version of the timetable is published in the approved data standard, with a user-friendly version and the statement that it has effect
It contains every date regulation 4 requires, and the dates show how the plan will be adopted within 30 months
It was published before or on the same day as the notice of intention to commence
A monthly check and a same-day update process are in place, and it does not need full council approval each time
A project initiation document exists covering scope, engagement strategy, detailed project planning, governance, resources and skills, funding, and risks with mitigations
The plan is resourced and financed to deliver the timetable
Risks are identified with processes to monitor, manage and mitigate them
All relevant teams and decision makers have designed, tested and signed off the approach, and delegations are agreed for efficient sign-off at key stages
The notice of intention to commence was published at least four months before the intended Gateway 1 date, as text on a webpage
The scoping consultation invited the appropriate general and specific consultation bodies, asked what the plan should contain and how to engage, and has closed
A community engagement strategy exists, with regard to government guidance, in the PID
Processes are in place to maximise responses from a diverse range of stakeholders, digital-first and traditional
Key decision makers have given feedback on the strategy
The proposed scope of the plan is understood from monitoring of the existing plan, baselining and early engagement
A draft vision exists and measurable outcomes are being identified
Evidence needs are mostly identified and scoped, with a delivery plan
The likely level of development required is starting to be understood (local housing need under the standard method, other needs)
Early high-level spatial options and topics needing specific policies have been considered
Whether SEA is required has been confirmed (expected for all local plans)
The relevant environmental protection objectives at international, national and community level are identified
Baseline information against which to assess the plan is identified: environmental characteristics of areas likely to be affected, existing problems and key receptors
Today is at least four months after the notice and after the scoping consultation closed, and within five years of adopting the existing plan (or the transitional deadline)
The self-assessment summary is written to the template, 150 to 250 words a section, with links and a sign-up for updates
The timetable will be updated the same day to record the publication date

checklists.title: Gateway 2 submission pack
checklists.intro: What the Planning Inspectorate asks for, and what it suggests, at Gateway 2. The Regulations leave the content to you; the procedural guide is specific about what makes the assessment useful.

items.text: The summary of consultation on proposed plan content and evidence is published (the gateway cannot start before the day after)
The Planning Inspectorate was given at least three months' notice through the timetable
Suggested dates and a venue for the two-day workshop are included
Covering letter: stage reached, activity since the last consultation, up to five key issues, consultation issues to flag, and a list of documents
Up-to-date local plan timetable
Project initiation document
Draft statement of compliance
Draft statement of soundness
Notice of intention to commence local plan preparation
Scoping consultation documents and the summary of feedback
Gateway 1 self-assessment summary
Proposed plan content and evidence consultation documents and their summary
Topic papers on the up-to-five issues (2,000 words each, cross-referencing evidence, with representations raising concerns and your response)
Full list of evidence base documents with expected completion dates
Draft vision, aims and objectives and up to 10 draft outcomes
Spatial strategy options or a draft spatial strategy
Latest draft plan and/or policies map
Progress towards the housing requirement: housing needs assessment, strategic housing market assessment, trajectory, site-selection methodology
Progress on Traveller accommodation needs and supply
Progress on other development needs (employment, retail) and supply
Site selection approach and evidence
Draft Green Belt review, where there is Green Belt
Evidence of engagement with infrastructure providers, neighbouring authorities and other bodies
Progress on the SEA and Habitats Regulations assessments, how the statutory agencies are involved and how the assessments inform the plan
The observations and advice and everything sent to the assessor are made available on the same day
Everyone who asked to be notified is notified, and a copy goes to each person identified in the advice
The timetable is revised the same day
The plan is revised having regard to the advice before the proposed plan consultation

checklists.title: Gateway 3: documents and prescribed requirements
checklists.intro: The gateway does not start until every submission document is provided, and the assessor must be satisfied on each of the twelve prescribed requirements in regulation 32.

guidance.label: Gateway 3 for local plans: what you need to do

items.text: The summary of consultation on the proposed local plan is published
Political approvals for submission are secured — passing obliges submission
The Inspectorate was given three months' notice
The proposed local plan you intend to submit
Map of proposed local plan policies
Statement of compliance
Statement of soundness
Statement summarising all consultation and engagement activities
Summary of scoping consultation
Summary of consultation on proposed plan content and evidence
Summary of consultation on the proposed local plan
Copies of any SDS conformity representations (where regulation 28 applies)
Statement of practical arrangements demonstrating readiness for examination
Supplementary plans statement (where regulation 29 applies)
The environmental report — or the regulation 9 statement of reasons if no SEA is required
Anything else needed to support the assessment: representations on the prescribed requirements with responses, how Gateway 2 advice was addressed, a statement of any post-consultation changes
(a) The plan sets out policies on the amount, type, location and timetable of development in the area
(b) It contains a vision relating to the area's characteristics, no more than ten measurable outcomes, and identifies superseded policies (or the statement of compliance explains why not)
(c) It is designed so that use and development of land contributes to mitigating and adapting to climate change
(d) It takes account of any local nature recovery strategy for the area
(e) It takes account of an assessment of the amount and type of housing needed, including affordable housing
(f) It includes nothing not permitted or required by section 15C(3) to (5) or (10) or regulation 11
(g) Observations and advice were sought at the times prescribed for Gateway 2 and Gateway 3
(h) The Gateway 2 observations and advice were published as required
(i) Regard has been had to the section 15CA(6) matters and the regulation 14 matters
(j) The examination submission documents in regulation 34(1)(a) and (c) to (i) are prepared
(k) The map of proposed policies accurately illustrates where the area-specific policies apply
(l) The authority is ready to proceed to independent examination
A suitably qualified programme officer is in post by the start of the gateway, with enough time for the whole examination
An examination website that complies with the Inspectorate's guidance will be available on submission
A suitable hearing venue is available for the anticipated dates
Video-conferencing facilities can host virtual sessions if needed
Staff, consultancy and specialist support are available for the examination's duration
The programme officer and staff are available for a focused period after the hearings for main modifications
The observations and advice are made available as soon as reasonably practicable, those who asked are notified, and copies go to anyone identified
On success: the gateway 3 completion statement and the submission documents are made available the same day
The timetable is revised the same day
On failure: the reasoned justification is addressed, updated documents are resubmitted, and the timetable records the resubmission date

checklists.title: Submission for examination
checklists.intro: Regulation 34 lists what goes to the Secretary of State with the plan, and what must be published and notified afterwards.

items.text: Map of proposed local plan policies
Gateway 3 completion statement
Statement summarising consultation and engagement
Summary of consultation on the proposed local plan
Copies of SDS conformity representations, where any were made
Statement of compliance
Statement of soundness
Environmental report, or the regulation 9 statement of reasons
Supporting documents necessary to demonstrate soundness
A statement of any changes since Gateway 3 and whether they were consulted on
A statement of the submission date is published on the website
The plan and every submitted document are made available, with a statement of where and when they can be inspected
Everyone who asked to be notified of submission is notified
Submission was within three weeks of the Gateway 3 report, or the Inspectorate was told why not
The programme officer is in contact with the Inspector and the hearing dates and venue are being confirmed
The examination website is live with every submission document
The process to publish hearing details at least six weeks before hearings open is ready

checklists.title: Adoption
checklists.intro: What has to happen once the Inspector's report arrives and the plan is adopted.

guidance.label: 30-month overview: adopt plan and publish policies map

items.text: The fact-check was returned within five days and the report and schedule of modifications are consistent
The recommendations and reasons are published as soon as reasonably practicable, made available, and those who asked are notified
The timetable is revised the same day
Full council has resolved to adopt the plan, with the recommended main modifications
The adopted plan is made available in a searchable electronic format
An adoption statement is made available with the date, modifications, inspection details, the date the next plan must begin, and the section 113 challenge right, grounds and period
A copy of the adoption statement is sent to everyone who asked to be notified of adoption
The Planning Inspectorate is told the plan is adopted
The plan, the environmental report and the SEA statement are published on a website that allows free download

The SEA statement covers: how environmental considerations were integrated, how the report and opinions were taken into account, the reasons for choosing the plan over the reasonable alternatives, and the monitoring measures
The consultation bodies and public consultees are informed of adoption and where the documents are
The policies map is prepared immediately after adoption and no later than one month after
It is based on Ordnance Survey mapping, has a key, illustrates every area-specific policy in the development plan and lists every plan-wide policy
It illustrates made neighbourhood plans as soon as reasonably practicable
It is made available, and each future revision is publicised the same day with the date and a description
Annual monitoring and SEA monitoring arrangements are in place
The date the next plan must begin by (five years from adoption) is in the diary and the timetable
